subject: Biology
title: Biophysics of Resting Membrane Potential (Vm) & Nernst/GHK Mechanics
learningObjectives: Identify resting ionic concentrations (Na+, K+, Cl-, A-) across the axolemma
Calculate equilibrium potentials using the Nernst Equation
Explain how passive K+ leak channels and the electrogenic Na+/K+ ATPase maintain Vm ≈ -70 mV
content:
An unstimulated neuron maintains a stable negative electrical charge across its plasma membrane termed the **Resting Membrane Potential ($V_m \approx -70\text{ mV}$)**, with the inner axoplasmic surface negatively charged relative to the outer extracellular fluid (ECF).

```
                      RESTING MEMBRANE IONIC GRADIENTS
                      
   EXTRACELLULAR FLUID (ECF): High [Na⁺] (~145 mM), High [Cl⁻] (~110 mM)
   ======================================================================= (Axolemma)
   AXOPLASM (Cytosol):         High [K⁺] (~140 mM), High [Negatively Charged Proteins]

                     MAINTENANCE OF RESTING POTENTIAL (Vm = -70 mV)
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
  DIFFERENTIAL MEMBRANE PERMEABILITY                          Na⁺/K⁺ ATPASE PUMP
  ├── Axolemma is 20–100× MORE PERMEABLE to K⁺                ├── Active primary transport
  │   than to Na⁺ at rest (via passive Leak K⁺ Channels).     └── Pumps 3 Na⁺ OUT and
  └── Impermeable to internal negative proteins (A⁻).             Pumps 2 K⁺ IN per ATP.
```

### 3.1 Electrochemical Equilibrium & Nernst Equation

The equilibrium potential ($E_X$) for any single ion species is calculated using the **Nernst Equation** ($T = 37^\circ\text{C}$):

$$E_X = \frac{R T}{z F} \ln \left( \frac{[X]_{\text{outside}}}{[X]_{\text{inside}}} \right) = \frac{61.5}{z} \log_{10} \left( \frac{[X]_{\text{outside}}}{[X]_{\text{inside}}} \right)$$

- **Potassium Equilibrium ($E_K$)**: $\approx -90\text{ mV}$.
- **Sodium Equilibrium ($E_{Na}$)**: $\approx +60\text{ mV}$.
- **Chloride Equilibrium ($E_{Cl}$)**: $\approx -70\text{ mV}$.
- **Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz (GHK) Equation**: Because resting axolemmal permeability to $\text{K}^+$ ($P_K$) is $20\text{--}100\times$ higher than to $\text{Na}^+$ ($P_{Na}$), the steady-state resting potential ($V_m \approx -70\text{ mV}$) sits far closer to $E_K$ ($-90\text{ mV}$) than to $E_{Na}$ ($+60\text{ mV}$).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Electrogenic Nature of the Na+/K+ Pump
conceptBreakdown.explanation: The Na+/K+ ATPase transports 3 positive charges out for every 2 positive charges brought in per ATP, creating a net outward current that directly hyperpolarizes the membrane by ~3 to 5 mV while sustaining concentration gradients.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Ouabain & Digitalis Inhibition
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Cardiac glycosides (Ouabain, Digoxin) specifically bind and inhibit the extracellular alpha-subunit of the Na+/K+ ATPase, dissipating ionic gradients and causing gradual cell depolarization.
